title: Container With Most Water
statement: Given n non-negative integers where each value represents a point at index i on the y-axis, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum amount of water.

examples.explanation: Choosing lines at index 1 (height 8) and index 8 (height 7) holds 7 * 8 = 49.

hints.content: You are scanning from both ends of one array. Which pattern always moves one of two pointers?
The area is the shorter line times the width. If you keep the shorter line, can any later container beat it?
No. Every container that still uses the shorter line has a smaller width and therefore a smaller area. So the shorter line can be discarded.

left = 0, right = n - 1
best = 0
while left < right:
    best = max(best, min(height[left], height[right]) * (right - left))
    if height[left] < height[right]: left++
    else: right--
Move the pointer at the shorter line. Moving the taller one would only produce smaller widths against the same bottleneck.

invariant: Every container skipped by moving a pointer was provably smaller than one already evaluated, so the best value is never lost.
whyThisPattern: The array is not sorted, but the decision does not need it. Comparing the two ends tells you which line is the bottleneck, and the bottleneck line cannot appear in a better container. That is the two pointers decision rule: move the pointer that cannot improve the answer.
bruteForce: Try every pair of lines: O(n^2). At n = 100,000 that is about 5 * 10^9 comparisons. Two pointers evaluate at most n containers, which is 50,000 times fewer.
interviewExplanation: I start one pointer at each end and evaluate the area as the shorter height times the distance. Then I move the pointer at the shorter line, because any container that keeps that line has a smaller width and can never beat the one I just measured. Each step discards one line permanently, giving O(n) time and O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Moving the pointer at the taller line, which only ever produces smaller areas.
Using the absolute difference instead of the smaller height.
Forgetting that width is right - left, not the number of elements between the lines.

animationSteps.title: What is the area?
animationSteps.description: Area = shorter line x distance between the lines.
animationSteps.text: The amount of water is the smaller of the two heights multiplied by the distance between the two lines.

animationSteps.title: Widest container
animationSteps.description: Start with the far ends: height 1 and height 7.
animationSteps.text: Left pointer at index 0 with height 1, right pointer at index 8 with height 7. The area is 1 times 8, which is 8.

animationSteps.title: Predict the move
animationSteps.description: left height 1, right height 7. Which pointer moves?
animationSteps.text: Left is 1 and right is 7. Choose which pointer should move next.

payload.prompt: left = 1, right = 7. Which line can be discarded?
payload.explanation: The shorter line is the bottleneck. Any narrower container keeps the same bottleneck and holds less water.

animationSteps.title: Move left
animationSteps.text: Left pointer moves to index 1 with height 8. The area becomes 7 times 7, which is 49, the best so far.

animationSteps.title: Now the right is shorter
animationSteps.description: right height 7 is smaller than left height 8, so right moves.
animationSteps.text: Left is 8 and right is 7, so the right pointer is the bottleneck and moves to index 7 with height 3.

animationSteps.title: Best area confirmed
animationSteps.text: The maximum area found is 49 from the lines at index 1 and index 8, and no later pair was larger.

payload.message: Maximum area 49 with pointers at index 1 and 8.
